title: A Protocol for the Implantation of a Permanent Window for High-Resolution Imaging of the Murine Lung
protocol: Conduct surgeries in a separate area within a lab, using a hood or laminar flow cabinet.
Set up three distinct zones: preparation, surgery, and recovery.
Wear a bouffant cap, mask, and clean lab coat at the start of each surgical session.
Sterilize all instruments and parts that will come into contact with the mouse during surgery.
Autoclave surgical instruments before use.
Rest sterilize instruments using a hot bead sterilizer for multiple surgeries.
Warm the surgical bed.
Turn on the bead sterilizer.
Wash hands with an antiseptic soap.
Put on sterile surgical gloves.
Change gloves if another animal is handled or between animals in multiple surgeries.
Tie a 2-inch length of 2-0 silk suture to the base of the 22-gauge catheter.
Anesthetize the mouse with 5% isoflurane.
Apply sterile ophthalmic ointment in both eyes to prevent drying and possible corneal damage.
Administer a pre-operative injection of 10 µL (0.1 mg/kg) buprenorphine diluted in 90 µL of sterile PBS subcutaneously to provide sufficient perioperative analgesia.
Shave the upper left chest incision site, generally an area approximately three times the size of the proposed incision should be shaved.
Nair the mouse’s upper chest from the sternum to the left back.
Intubate the mouse with a 22 gauge catheter following either the published protocol by Das et al. or by DuPage et al.
Test to make sure that the lungs inflate bilaterally using the lung inflation bulb.
Tie the 2-0 silk suture around the mouse’s snout, securing the intubation catheter under the mouse’s upper incisors.
Transfer the mouse onto the heated surgical platform and place the mouse in the right lateral decubitus position exposing the left thorax.
Connect the 22 gauge catheter to the ventilator.
Let the mouse’s breathing stabilize for one minute and lower isofluorane to 3%.
Periodically check for nervous response via a toe pinch test.
Check the health and vitality of the mouse by observing natural respiration and lung tissue color once the thoracic cavity has been breached.
Tape the mouse's front paws cranially, back paws caudally, and place one piece of tape down the posterior ridge to the operating table for stabilization and optimal exposure.
Open the sterile instruments inside the hood.
Sterilize the mouse skin with antiseptic.
Define the point of implantation by measuring 7 mm laterally from the sternum and 7 mm superior of the last left rib.
Lift the skin with Graefe forceps and cut a 10 mm circular incision through the skin.
Isolate the main vessels and cauterize them at both ends with the electrocautery pen.
Remove soft tissue, including the mammary fat pad and muscle overlaying the ribs.
With Graefe forceps, pick up rib 6 or 7 toward the center of the lung.
Insert one blade of the blunt micro-dissecting scissors with the rounded side down through the muscle between ribs 6 & 7 to breach thoracic seal.
Block the expiratory tube to the ventilator to collapse the lung.
Cut a 5 mm circular hole in the rib cage.
Make a purse-string stitch with 5-0 silk suture ~1 mm from the edge of the hole, interlacing with the ribs.
Fit the window frame into the space with ribs/muscle fitting snugly within the grooved edge of the window frame.
Tie the suture three times in a locking knot.
Place approximately 100 µL of cyanoacrylate adhesive into a 1 mL insulin syringe.
Gently apply a stream of compressed air to the lung tissue for ~10-20 seconds to dry the tissue.
Grasp the outside edge of the window frame and lift the frame and the chest wall to create ample space between the surface of the lung and the underbelly of the window frame.
Use the insulin syringe to place a small amount of cyanoacrylate adhesive along the entire underbelly of the ring.
Inflate the lung by increasing the positive end expiratory pressure (PEEP) on the ventilator.
Gently press the window frame onto the lung tissue and hold for 10-20 seconds.
Dispense the remainder of the cyanoacrylate adhesive in the syringe onto a rectangular coverslip, forming a 5 mm drop.
Using the Vacuum Pick-Up System with Pump, pick up the 5 mm coverslip.
Dip the coverslip into the cyanoacrylate adhesive and scrape off excess against the edge of the cover glass three times.
Place the coverslip into the window frame recess bringing it in contact with the exposed lung surface.
Keep gentle pressure applied until the cyanoacrylate adhesive is set (at least 25 seconds).
Lower isoflurane to 0%.
Use 5-0 silk suture to place a second purse-string stitch <1 mm from the cut edge of the dermis surrounding the window.
Tighten the suture and use both Graefe forceps to tuck the skin under the top rim of the window.
Cinch the purse string stitch and tie using three locking knots.
Remove residual air from the thoracic cavity by inserting a new sterile insulin syringe just under the xiphoid process pointing towards the left shoulder to penetrate through the diaphragm.
Draw back the plunger to remove air.
Remove tape from all paws and back.
Cut the 2-0 silk suture tying the intubation catheter to the snout, but allow mouse to continue being ventilated with 100% oxygen.
When the mouse is nearly ready to wake up (starting to twitch and move), extubate the mouse and move to a clean cage.
Continue to allow the mouse to recover under a heat lamp.
If the animal displays any signs of distress, euthanize following approved protocols.
Once the mouse becomes more active, inject with another dose of 10 µL buprenorphine for analgesic.
Add 10 mL of oral antibiotic solution in 250 mL of drinking water.
Check the health and condition of the mouse daily.
Provide a 10 µL (0.1 mg/kg) buprenorphine injection daily.
Apply antibiotic ointment every day or two to skin surrounding the implanted window.
